text:
Asha (CS): FYI — we got the post-mortem request from BigRetail for last night's outage. They're asking for a concise timeline and what we're doing to prevent recurrence.
Tom (oncall): I'm putting together notes from the paging timeline. Root cause looks like the autoscaler mis-evaluating queued KV-cache evictions after the config flip.
Riley (SRE): Confirmed. Sequence: 22:03 deploy of autoscale policy change -> 22:09 spike in prefix cache evictions -> 22:11 queue backlog -> 22:13 throttling cascade on rtx-pool-3 -> 22:18 partial 503s.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-432 started at 1765430580. Pager routed to @Tom, @Riley. Post-incident follow-up requested by #customer-success.
Asha (CS): Can we draft a customer-facing RCA (1 page) + a technical appendix? They want something short to share with their engineering leaders.
Claire (PM): Short version should include cause, impact (regions + % of requests), customer-visible remediation, and three preventative actions with timelines.
Tom (oncall): For impact numbers: roughly 18: 22:13–22:22 degraded across eu-west and us-central. About ~7% of requests returned 5xx during window. Need exact metric from observability. @Riley can you confirm?
Riley (SRE): Pulling metrics now — got it: 7.4% error rate spike, 92nd percentile latency doubled for affected models. Geo breakdown: eu-west ~55% of affected errors, us-central ~40%, APAC negligible.
Marta (Support): BigRetail said they saw session drops for their batch embeddings job; they lost three runs. They want clarity on whether data was retried.
Tom (oncall): We retried a subset automatically; some client jobs failed before we triggered fallback. We'll state that we attempted automatic retries and that we're offering to re-run their failed jobs free of charge.
Asha (CS): Drafting the customer note now. Proposal: short heading, one-paragraph summary, timeline in bullets, mitigation already applied, preventative actions + offer of 1-month credit and free reruns. Want review before I send.
Claire (PM): Sounds good. Suggest we add that Dedicated customers can pin autoscale policies and we can schedule a review to help them tune.
Riley (SRE): Preventative actions to propose: 1) Revert flawed autoscale heuristic + add safety cap by 2026-05-01. 2) Add an early-warning anomaly trigger for prefix eviction rate by 2026-04-10. 3) Add automated cross-region fallbacks to rim-model-compat by 2026-04-20 (risk mitigations in canary).
Tom (oncall): Also adding runbook edits: explicit on-call trigger for cache-eviction alarms, and a short rollback playbook cached in the PagerDuty incident notes.
Asha (CS): Here's my draft customer message — please comment inline:
```
Hi BigRetail team —

Short summary: On 2026-04-10 at ~22:13 UTC, Redwood experienced a brief degradation affecting text-generation endpoints which produced increased errors and latency for some model endpoints. We identified a misconfigured autoscaling policy that caused excessive KV-cache evictions and a request backlog.

Impact: ~7.4% of requests for affected models returned errors between 22:13–22:22 UTC; customers in eu-west and us-central saw the majority of impact.

What we did: Our on-call team reverted the autoscale change within 5 minutes and applied a temporary throttle to cache evictions to stabilize the service. Traffic recovered to baseline by 22:22 UTC.

Next steps and fixes: We will (1) revert the autoscale heuristic permanently and replace it with a safer policy, (2) implement an eviction-rate anomaly alarm, (3) add cross-region fallback routing for critical models. We estimate these changes will be completed by the dates shared below.

We will credit affected usage and offer to rerun failed jobs. If you'd like, we can schedule a technical call to walk through the timeline and the fixes.

Apologies for the disruption — we take reliability seriously and are working to prevent recurrence.
```
Asha (CS): Comments?
Claire (PM): Add a short line clarifying "no customer data was exposed or persisted due to this incident" if it's accurate. That's often a top ask.
Riley (SRE): Accurate — no data exfiltration, only transient failures. Add that line. Also propose adding the estimated completion dates after engineering sync.
Tom (oncall): Small wording nit: change "reverted the autoscale change within 5 minutes" -> "reverted the autoscale policy change within ~5 minutes of detection" (more precise).
Marta (Support): Also include contact: cs@redwood.ai and a dedicated sync link, and offer for us to coordinate re-runs.
Asha (CS): Updated draft with those edits. Ready to send after final ack. Who can sign off for SRE? @Riley?
Riley (SRE): Ack for technical content. I'll attach the timeline metrics snapshot (to be included as an appendix).
Tom (oncall): Ack from on-call. I'll add a note to the incident ticket describing the rollback commands used:
```
# rollback snippet
kubectl apply -f autoscale-policy-prev.yaml -n inference
# temporary throttle
kubectl patch cm kv-cache-config -n inference --patch '{"evictionThrottle":true}'
```
Asha (CS): Thanks — I'll send the note to BigRetail and copy the execs. I'll also prepare a separate internal RCA summary for our account team and create an internal comms template for future incidents.
Claire (PM): Please attach the SLO impact numbers and the proposed timeline for the three fixes. We should also add an item to the product roadmap to surface autoscale policy warnings in the Console.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-432: Post-incident follow-up filed by Asha (CS). Next action: send customer note and create internal RCA doc.
Marta (Support): If you want, I can propose a short customer-friendly subject line: "Update: Service Disruption on 2026-04-10 — Redwood Summary & Next Steps"
Asha (CS): Perfect — sending now. Will upload the internal RCA to the ticket after the metrics snapshot is attached. Thanks all.
